doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: Baquet great uncles: George and Theo Baquet
summary: His mother's family, the Baquets, included clarinetist George Baquet and Theo Baquet, who went to New York in 1919.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: was Baquet which is a French name — B-A-Q-U-E-T — George Baquet was a very famous clarinet player who played in the twenties and the thirties, in fact he was one of the teachers of a great saxophone player and a clarinet player from New Orleans called Sidney Bechet. So my great uncle.
I’ll be darned. That was your great uncle.

My great uncle, yeah. And he had brothers, like Theo Baquet, who played clarinet, who left New Orleans in 1919 and came up to New York and was playing with Jimmy Durante back in those days man. That’s my great uncle. I never did meet him but you know, that’s part of my history man. So like I say I’m rich.
